question: What is the meaning of building type in relation to building infromation?
description: The building type refers to the classification of a building based on its purpose, design, or construction method. It is an essential aspect of building information, as it helps in organizing and managing the various components and features of a building. The building type can influence the selection of materials, the design of systems, and the overall functionality of the building. In the context of sustainable construction, understanding the building type is crucial for identifying opportunities to improve energy efficiency, reduce waste, and promote environmental sustainability. For example, a building type such as a residential building may require different materials and systems than a commercial building, and understanding these differences can help in designing more sustainable and efficient buildings.

The international basic standards for linked data contain technical 
specifications for the data formats to be used and the correct design of 
exchangeable information structures. NEN 2660-2 provides a detailed 
elaboration of these standards for information structures applied to 
the construction sector. 
Other initiatives, such as IMBOR (Informatiemodel Beheer Openbare 
Ruimte - Public Space Management Information Model), CB-NL 
(Conceptenbibliotheek Nederland - Dutch library of concepts) and 
Rioned can be linked to these information structures.  
A further explanation of technical specifications, including a practical 
example based on the Longlist of Attributes, can be found in Annex C 
‘On the way to data interoperability’.
